Q1: Docusate sodium exhibits known significant hazards for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), oral exposure (ORL), and dermal/eye contact (SKN) at Tier 1. It also presents expanded environmental concerns (ENV Tier 2) and demonstrated low/moderate inhalation hazards (IHL Tier 3). However, data for endocrine disruption (EDC) and organ/systemic hazards (OGN) are currently deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Docusate sodium is listed on the SCIL Yellow Triangle list, indicating it meets Safer Choice Criteria for its function but still presents some hazard profile issues, meaning it is not considered of low concern across all human health and environmental endpoints. It is not currently found on any lists specifically designating it as a low-hazard chemical.
Q3: With 21,000 literature references, Docusate sodium is exceptionally well-studied within our dataset of fracking and petrochemical materials, far exceeding the median. Its molecular formula is precisely defined as C20H38O7S.Na, and it is not classified as an incompletely defined substance, further affirming its clear characterization. Although two hazard classes (endocrine disruption and organ/systemic hazards) are data deficient, the overall robust body of literature suggests a largely complete hazard profile.
